title: Budget-aware dashboard tiling for multi-tenant conversational inference
content:
Purpose
---
Capture a succinct, actionable guide for composing dashboards used by operators and product teams that must balance visibility with query cost. Focus: conversational inference (chat sessions, streaming, embeddings used for reranking) across multiple tenants where token economics matter.

Context & problem statement
---
- Dashboards are growing expensive: large trace captures and wide-window aggregations spike query cost and SLI query budgets.
- Ops wants high-fidelity tail latency + KV-warmth signals for hot tenants. PMs want simple health panels per product route. Finance wants per-tenant cost attribution.
- Need guardrails for tile selection, aggregation windows, trace sampling, and a lightweight investigation path that reduces on-demand heavy queries.

Audience
---
- Oncall operators (SRE/ops)
- Serving/runtime engineers
- Product owners for chat/embedding routes
- Cost/finance analysts

Design goals (explicit)
---
1) Keep an average dashboard cost <= 0.5 query-budget-unit per 5-min refresh (heuristic).
2) Provide a 3-click investigation path from high-level SLO panel to detailed trace or prompt replay.
3) Protect privacy and avoid full prompt/text capture for traces in production.
4) Provide per-tenant cost signal and a tenant-priority view for investigators.

Core metric definitions (compact)
---
- convo_ttf_token_ms: Time (ms) from request ingress to first token emitted. Aggregation: p50/p95/p99 over 5m. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. SLO: p95 < 180ms for premium tenants.
- token_emit_rate: tokens/s emitted per route. Aggregation window: 1m moving. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. Usage: normalization for cost panels.
- kv_prefix_hit_rate: fraction of requests where prefix/KV cache returned >50% of KV items needed. Formula: kv_hits / kv_lookups. Owner: eng-caching. Target: >0.6 for warm cohorts.
- per_tenant_token_cost: estimated $ per 1k tokens for tenant = token_count * model_cost_per_token (derived). Owner: finance+obs. Note: derived, stored in daily rollup to avoid expensive real-time joins.
- rerank_sli_quality_delta: fraction of reranked responses with regression flag from eval probe. Owner: product-hosted-api. Window: daily.

Trace/span annotation requirements
---
Minimal set to capture in production traces (avoid prompt text):
- span tags: tenant_id, route, model_variant, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, token_count, kv_cache_hit (boolean), kvcache_hit_fraction (float), first_token_ms, backend_queue_ms, gpu_exec_ms.
- session_id + short_request_id (8-char hex) to stitch traces into session view.
- sampling policy: adaptive. Always sample all requests with per_tenant_token_cost > $0.01 or first_token_ms > 500ms. Otherwise probabilistic sample 0.5% default; bump to 5% during recent SLI regressions.
- redaction: do NOT capture prompt_text or user_message. If replay needed, use prompt-hash + length and retrieve from secure replay store (access-controlled) only for gated investigations.

Dashboard tiling & panel rules (practical checklist)
---
1) Tier panels into L0/L1/L2: L0 = critical SLOs (p95 TTF, error rate, capacity headroom). L1 = cost-normalized metrics (per_tenant_token_cost, avg tokens/req). L2 = investigative (trace density, kv-prefetch heatmaps).
2) Tile sizing: keep L0 to a single 2x1 row per route group. L1 can be 2x2. L2 panels should be behind an investigator-only toggle.
3) Aggregation windows: default 5m for L0, 15m for L1, 1h for L2 historical overviews.
4) Query budget caps: dashboards must declare an estimated query_cost_per_refresh in the dashboard meta. If estimate > threshold, require approval.
5) Avoid wide GROUP BY across tenant_id on live panels. Use pre-aggregated rollups (daily_hourly) or sampled top-N tenants.
6) Costed widgets: any panel that uses full token logs must use sampled keys and link to a traced investigation, not be on default online dashboards.
7) Tenant-priority lane: show a dynamic cut of top-20 tenants by token spend with sparklines. Full tenant drilldowns are a separate drill page to avoid monthly query costs.

Investigation flow (operator playbook)
---
1) Alert fires on L0 p95 TTF. Operator opens tenant-priority lane and checks if one tenant dominates.
2) If single-tenant: open tenant rollup (pre-agg) -> check kv_prefix_hit_rate and token_emit_rate. If kv hit low, suspect cold cache.
3) If multi-tenant wide spikes: check routing/burst panel and capacity headroom. If headroom issue, trigger autoscale/capacity fallback.
4) For suspected model slowness: use sampled trace set (adaptive-sample) and inspect span durations (gpu_exec_ms vs backend_queue_ms).
5) For quality regressions, proxy to rerank_sli_quality_delta and linked eval runs.

Sampling & cost controls (implementation notes)
---
- Adaptive sampling policy implemented as a small service in front of trace collector: evaluates per-request heuristic (cost, latency, tenant priority) and tags span.sample=true.
- Store sampled prompt hashes + metadata in a small secure store (for gated retrieval). Avoid storing raw prompts.
- Allow on-demand heavier trace captures for a specific tenant for up to 30 minutes via a ticketed self-serve button in console (requires SRE approval). Logs the Jira ticket id.

Dashboard maintenance & governance
---
- Every dashboard must include: owner, estimated query_cost_per_refresh, last_cost_estimate_date, lightweight runbook (2–4 lines), and change log entry.
- Quarterly review: retire panels that exceed cost/utility threshold. Runbook: 'panel -> owner -> review -> retire/optimize'.

Open questions / decisions
---
- How to surface per-model-cost-per-token in real time without expensive joins? (current idea: use a lightweight cache service with TTL 5m)
- Do we permit full-text prompt capture in non-prod only? (agreement leaning: yes, staging only)
- Approval flow for on-demand full traces: simple Slack+ticket vs console gated workflow?

Action items (owners & tickets)
---
- Asha: prototype adaptive sampler config and doc PR (linear OBS-521).
- Diego: add estimated query_cost_per_refresh to the dashboard schema and run migration for top-50 dashboards (linear OBS-523).
- Sofia: implement tenant-priority lane widget and pre-agg API (linear OBS-525).
- Michael: audit top-100 dashboards for GROUP BY tenant_id and flag (linear OBS-527).

Notes to reviewers
---
- This is intended as a living doc for Q4 telemetry sprint. Keep language prescriptive but pragmatic — goal is to reduce ops query costs by 30% without losing investigability.
- If you have existing cost-estimation formulas in other docs, link them into linked_artifacts.

References
---
